members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Python's default pickle path calls cls(*self.args), but MCPError stores only the message string in self.args (via super().__init__(error.message)), causing TypeError on unpickle because the constructors expect typed objects (ErrorData for MCPError, (elicitations, message) for UrlElicitationRequiredError). All three PRs add __reduce__ methods to fix this same reconstruction mismatch. (3 PRs)

members.cluster_pick_reason: PR #2703 is the only PR that fixes both MCPError and UrlElicitationRequiredError in a single change, using direct __reduce__ methods on each class with no intermediate helper layer. PR #2478 only partially addresses the base class and introduces a module-level _restore_mcp_error indirection that adds complexity without benefit. PR #2555 is a partial fix — it only covers UrlElicitationRequiredError and leaves MCPError broken. PR #2703's approach of returning (self.__class__, (self.error,)) for MCPError is the cleanest: it passes the full ErrorData object directly, matching __init__'s actual signature. Note: #2703 targets a different index base (4943114912 vs f153ea319d for the other two), so the test coverage from #2555 should be cherry-picked in alongside it.

clusters.pick_reason: PR #2703 is the only PR that fixes both MCPError and UrlElicitationRequiredError in a single change, using direct __reduce__ methods on each class with no intermediate helper layer. PR #2478 only partially addresses the base class and introduces a module-level _restore_mcp_error indirection that adds complexity without benefit. PR #2555 is a partial fix — it only covers UrlElicitationRequiredError and leaves MCPError broken. PR #2703's approach of returning (self.__class__, (self.error,)) for MCPError is the cleanest: it passes the full ErrorData object directly, matching __init__'s actual signature. Note: #2703 targets a different index base (4943114912 vs f153ea319d for the other two), so the test coverage from #2555 should be cherry-picked in alongside it.

members.title: fix(shared): preserve MCPError payload on pickle
members.author: MukundaKatta
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2703: Python's default pickle path calls cls(*self.args), but MCPError stores only the message string in self.args (via super().__init__(error.message)), causing TypeError on unpickle because the constructors expect typed objects (ErrorData for MCPError, (elicitations, message) for UrlElicitationRequiredError). All three PRs add __reduce__ methods to fix this same reconstruction mismatch.

members.title: fix: don't send a response for cancelled requests
members.author: Zelys-DFKH
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2514: RequestResponder.cancel() violates the MCP spec: it sent an error response for cancelled requests instead of emitting a CancelledNotification. PR #2493 removes the incorrect error-response path (both in RequestResponder.cancel() and the server's _handle_request handler). PR #2514 adds the affirmative spec-compliant behavior — importing CancelledNotificationParams and restructuring cancel() to send the proper notification on timeout/caller-cancellation. Both PRs are editing the same function for the same protocol-compliance reason.
